subskill: area of a rectangle, with perimeter available
prompt: A rectangular patio is 14 feet long and 6 feet wide. What is the area of the patio, in square feet?
explanation: The area of a rectangle is length times width, 14 x 6 = 84 square feet. "40" is the perimeter, 2(14 + 6), which is a length rather than an area. "42" comes from a solver who uses the triangle formula and takes half the product, (1/2)(14)(6). "20" comes from a solver who adds the two dimensions, 14 + 6, instead of multiplying them.

subskill: third angle of a triangle from two given angles
prompt: In triangle ABC, the measure of angle A is 34° and the measure of angle B is 71°. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle C?
explanation: The three angle measures of a triangle add to 180°, so angle C measures 180 - 34 - 71 = 75 degrees. "146" is 180 - 34, from a solver who subtracts only angle A. "109" is 180 - 71, from a solver who subtracts only angle B. "19" is 180 - 90 - 71, from a solver who assumes the triangle has a right angle and then discards the 34°.

subskill: finding an endpoint from a midpoint and the other endpoint
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, M(4,−1) is the midpoint of segment PQ, and point P has coordinates (−2,5). What are the coordinates of point Q?
explanation: Each coordinate of the midpoint is the average of the corresponding coordinates, so Q = (2(4) - (-2), 2(-1) - 5) = (10, -7). "(1, 2)" is the midpoint of P and M, from a solver who averages the two points given instead of extending past M. "(6, -6)" is M - P, the change from P to M, reported as though it were a location. "(-8, 11)" reverses the roles of P and M, computing 2P - M.

subskill: similar triangles in a shadow proportion
prompt: A person 6 feet tall casts a shadow 9 feet long. At the same moment, a nearby flagpole casts a shadow 42 feet long. How tall is the flagpole, in feet?
explanation: The two triangles are similar, so height/shadow is the same for both: the flagpole is 42 x (6/9) = 28 feet tall. "63" inverts the ratio, computing 42 x (9/6). "39" comes from a solver who reasons additively, taking the extra 33 feet of shadow and adding the person's 6 feet, 42 - 9 + 6. "33" is 42 - 9, the difference of the two shadow lengths reported as a height.

subskill: area of a trapezoid, with a slant side offered for the height
prompt: The figure below shows trapezoid ABCD, in which BC is parallel to AD. A dashed segment marks the height. All lengths are in centimeters. What is the area of ABCD, in square centimeters?

graphic.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 360 250" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#12151C"><polygon points="40,200 300,200 230,110 90,110" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="110" x2="90" y2="200" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="5,4"/><polyline points="90,188 102,188 102,200" fill="none" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="30" y="216">A</text><text x="302" y="216">D</text><text x="82" y="103">B</text><text x="232" y="103">C</text><text x="162" y="222">18</text><text x="155" y="103">10</text><text x="74" y="160">6</text><text x="44" y="150">8</text><text x="16" y="238" font-size="11" fill="#5A6474">Figure not drawn to scale.</text></svg>
graphic.caption: Figure not drawn to scale.

explanation: The area of a trapezoid is half the sum of the parallel sides times the height: (1/2)(18 + 10)(6) = 84 square centimeters. "168" is (18 + 10)(6), from a solver who omits the factor of one half. "108" is 18 x 6, treating the figure as a rectangle on the longer base. "112" uses the slant side 8 in place of the height 6, giving (1/2)(18 + 10)(8).

subskill: lateral surface area of a cylinder, with volume available
prompt: A cylindrical tank has a radius of 6 feet and a height of 10 feet. What is the lateral surface area of the tank — the curved side only, not the two circular ends — in square feet, in terms of π?
explanation: The curved side unrolls into a rectangle whose width is the circumference and whose height is the height of the tank: 2π(6)(10) = 120π square feet. "360π" is the volume, π(6²)(10), a different quantity. "192π" is the total surface area, 2π(6)(10) + 2π(6²), which includes the two ends the question excludes. "36π" is π(6²), the area of one circular end.

subskill: cosine of an acute angle in a right triangle
prompt: In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at C, AB = 25, and BC = 7. What is the value of cos A?
explanation: The leg adjacent to angle A is AC, and AC = √(25² - 7²) = 24, so cos A = 24/25. "7/25" is sin A, the leg opposite angle A over the hypotenuse. "7/24" is tan A, opposite over adjacent. "25/24" is the reciprocal of the correct ratio, from a solver who writes hypotenuse over adjacent.

distractor_solve.7/25: var opp=7, hyp=25; return opp + "/" + hyp;

subskill: total surface area of a rectangular solid
prompt: A closed rectangular box measures 5 inches by 8 inches by 3 inches. What is the total surface area of the box, in square inches?
explanation: The six faces pair up, so the surface area is 2(5x8 + 5x3 + 8x3) = 2(40 + 15 + 24) = 158 square inches. "79" is 40 + 15 + 24, the area of three faces only, from a solver who omits the factor of 2. "120" is 5 x 8 x 3, the volume rather than a surface area. "64" is 4(5 + 8 + 3), the total length of the twelve edges.

subskill: area remaining after a quarter circle is removed from a square
prompt: A square pane of glass measures 14 inches on each side. A quarter circle of radius 14 inches, centered at one corner of the square, is cut out and removed. Using 22/7 for π, what is the area of the piece that remains, in square inches?
explanation: The square has area 14² = 196, and the quarter circle has area (1/4)(22/7)(14²) = 154, so 196 - 154 = 42 square inches remain. "154" is the area of the piece that was removed rather than the piece that remains. "350" adds the two areas instead of subtracting, 196 + 154. "49" is 196/4, from a solver who removes a quarter of the square rather than a quarter of a circle.

subskill: solving for x from corresponding angles on parallel lines
prompt: In the figure below, lines l and m are parallel and are cut by transversal t. The two marked angles are corresponding angles. What is the value of x?

graphic.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 360 260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#12151C"><line x1="30" y1="80" x2="330" y2="80" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="30" y1="180" x2="330" y2="180" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="40" x2="270" y2="220" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="2"/><polyline points="170,72 178,80 170,88" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="1.5"/><polyline points="170,172 178,180 170,188" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="336" y="76">l</text><text x="334" y="176">m</text><text x="276" y="232">t</text><text x="142" y="68">(3x + 20)°</text><text x="242" y="170">(5x − 40)°</text><text x="16" y="248" font-size="11" fill="#5A6474">Figure not drawn to scale.</text></svg>
graphic.caption: Figure not drawn to scale.

explanation: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are congruent, so 3x + 20 = 5x - 40, which gives 2x = 60 and x = 30. "25" comes from a solver who treats the two angles as supplementary and solves 3x + 20 + 5x - 40 = 180. "110" is the measure of each marked angle, 3(30) + 20, which answers a question the item did not ask. "10" comes from a solver who subtracts in the wrong direction, solving 2x = 40 - 20.

subskill: area of similar figures from a ratio of perimeters
prompt: Two regular hexagons are similar. The ratio of the perimeter of the smaller hexagon to the perimeter of the larger hexagon is 3 to 5. The area of the smaller hexagon is 45 square inches. What is the area of the larger hexagon, in square inches?
explanation: Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding lengths, so the larger area is 45(5²/3²) = 45(25/9) = 125 square inches. "75" is 45(5/3), which scales by the ratio of lengths instead of by its square. "27" is 45(3/5), which applies the length ratio in the wrong direction as well. "81" is 45(9/5), from a solver who squares the 3 but leaves the 5 unsquared.

subskill: using cosine to find a leg from the hypotenuse and an acute angle
prompt: The figure below shows right triangle PQR, with the right angle at R. What is the length of PR, to the nearest tenth?

graphic.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 240" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#12151C"><polygon points="40,190 250,190 250,60" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="2"/><polyline points="238,190 238,178 250,178" fill="none" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M 70 190 A 30 30 0 0 0 66 176" fill="none" stroke="#0A5C48" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="30" y="206">P</text><text x="256" y="206">R</text><text x="256" y="58">Q</text><text x="74" y="182">35°</text><text x="128" y="116">18</text><text x="16" y="226" font-size="11" fill="#5A6474">Figure not drawn to scale.</text></svg>
graphic.caption: Figure not drawn to scale.

explanation: PR is the leg adjacent to the 35° angle and PQ is the hypotenuse, so PR = 18 cos 35° ≈ 14.7. "10.3" is 18 sin 35°, the length of the opposite leg QR. "12.6" is 18 tan 35°, from a solver who uses the tangent ratio with the hypotenuse in place of the adjacent leg. "22.0" is 18/cos 35°, from a solver who divides by the cosine rather than multiplying.

subskill: mean of a small data set, with the median available
prompt: A basketball player scored 82, 91, 76, 88, and 93 points in five games. What was the mean number of points she scored per game?
explanation: The five scores total 430, and 430/5 = 86 points per game. "88" is the median, the middle value once the scores are ordered, not the mean. "107.5" is 430/4, from a solver who divides by one fewer game than were played. "71.7" is 430/6, from a solver who divides by one more game than were played.

subskill: median of an even-sized list containing a repeated value
prompt: Six students reported the number of books they read last month: 12, 7, 15, 9, 7, and 20. What is the median of these six numbers?
explanation: In order the values are 7, 7, 9, 12, 15, 20. With six values the median is the average of the third and fourth, (9 + 12)/2 = 10.5. "11.7" is the mean, 70/6, rounded to the nearest tenth. "9" is the third value, from a solver who takes a single middle value even though the count is even. "7" is the mode, the value that occurs most often, not the median.

distractor_solve.7: var a=[12,7,15,9,7,20],best=a[0],bc=0; for(var i=0;i<a.length;i++){var c=0; for(var j=0;j<a.length;j++){ if(a[j]===a[i]) c++; } if(c>bc){bc=c;best=a[i];}} return best;

subskill: probability of a single draw from a three-colour set
prompt: A bag contains 4 red marbles, 7 blue marbles, and 9 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability that the marble drawn is blue, to the nearest hundredth?
explanation: There are 20 marbles in all and 7 of them are blue, so the probability is 7/20 = 0.35. "0.45" is 9/20, the probability of drawing green. "0.54" is 7/13, which compares the blue marbles to the 13 marbles that are not blue rather than to all 20. "0.20" is 4/20, the probability of drawing red.

subskill: probability of two draws without replacement
prompt: A drawer contains 5 black socks and 3 white socks. Two socks are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both socks drawn are black?
explanation: The first sock is black with probability 5/8, and then 4 of the remaining 7 socks are black, so the probability is (5/8)(4/7) = 20/56 = 5/14. "25/64" is (5/8)(5/8), which treats the first sock as replaced. "3/28" is (3/8)(2/7), the probability that both socks are white. "15/56" is (5/8)(3/7), the probability of drawing a black sock and then a white one.

distractor_solve.25/64: var num=5*5, den=8*8; return num + "/" + den;
distractor_solve.15/56: var num=5*3, den=8*7; return num + "/" + den;

subskill: weighted mean of two unequal groups
prompt: A shop sold 15 shirts at an average price of $76 and 5 jackets at an average price of $96. What was the average price, in dollars, of the 20 items sold?
explanation: The 20 items brought in 15(76) + 5(96) = 1,140 + 480 = 1,620 dollars, so the average price is 1,620/20 = 81 dollars. "86" is (76 + 96)/2, which averages the two group averages as though the groups were the same size. "108" is 1,620/15, from a solver who divides the full total by the number of shirts only. "57" is 1,140/20, from a solver who spreads only the shirt revenue over all 20 items.

subskill: fundamental counting principle over three choices
prompt: A sandwich shop offers 4 kinds of bread, 6 fillings, and 5 sauces. How many different sandwiches can be made using exactly one bread, one filling, and one sauce?
explanation: Each choice is made independently, so the count is 4 x 6 x 5 = 120 sandwiches. "15" is 4 + 6 + 5, from a solver who adds the three menus instead of multiplying them. "24" is 4 x 6, which counts bread-and-filling pairs and never reaches the sauces. "30" is 6 x 5, which counts filling-and-sauce pairs and never reaches the breads.

subskill: combinations, with the ordered count available
prompt: A committee of 3 people is to be chosen from a group of 8 people. How many different committees are possible?
explanation: There are 8 x 7 x 6 = 336 ordered ways to pick three people, and each committee is counted 3! = 6 times, so there are 336/6 = 56 committees. "336" is that ordered count, which treats two committees with the same members in a different order as different. "168" is 336/2, from a solver who divides by 2 rather than by 3!. "21" is 8 + 7 + 6, from a solver who adds the three factors instead of multiplying them.

subskill: conditional probability read from a two-way table
prompt: The table below shows the drink preference of the people who attended a book club, by session. Among the people who prefer tea, what is the probability that a randomly chosen one of them attends the evening session? Round to the nearest hundredth.

graphic.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 380 210" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#12151C"><text x="20" y="24" font-size="12" fill="#5A6474">Drink preference, by session</text><rect x="20" y="36" width="340" height="130" fill="none" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="20" y1="66" x2="360" y2="66" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="20" y1="136" x2="360" y2="136" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="130" y1="36" x2="130" y2="166" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="290" y1="36" x2="290" y2="166" stroke="#2B3A8C" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="150" y="58">Coffee</text><text x="228" y="58">Tea</text><text x="303" y="58">Total</text><text x="32" y="90">Morning</text><text x="160" y="90">48</text><text x="234" y="90">22</text><text x="312" y="90">70</text><text x="32" y="122">Evening</text><text x="160" y="122">34</text><text x="234" y="122">46</text><text x="312" y="122">80</text><text x="32" y="156">Total</text><text x="160" y="156">82</text><text x="234" y="156">68</text><text x="308" y="156">150</text></svg>

explanation: The condition restricts the group to the 68 people who prefer tea, of whom 46 attend the evening session, so the probability is 46/68 ≈ 0.68. "0.31" is 46/150, which divides by everyone surveyed instead of by the tea drinkers. "0.57" is 46/80, which conditions on the evening session rather than on tea. "0.45" is 68/150, the share of everyone surveyed who prefers tea, which answers a different question.

subskill: expected value of a spinner with a repeated outcome
prompt: A spinner has five sections of equal area, showing $2, $4, $4, $6, and $9. The spinner is spun once. What is the expected value, in dollars, of the amount shown?
explanation: Every section is equally likely, so the expected value is the mean of the five amounts: (2 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 9)/5 = 25/5 = 5 dollars. "4" is the median amount, and also the amount that appears most often, neither of which is the expected value. "7" is 9 - 2, the range of the amounts. "5.25" is (2 + 4 + 6 + 9)/4, from a solver who averages the four distinct amounts and so counts the repeated $4 section only once.

subskill: probability of at least one success over three trials
prompt: A fair coin is flipped 3 times. What is the probability that at least one of the flips lands heads?
explanation: There are 8 equally likely sequences of three flips, and only TTT has no heads, so 7 of the 8 sequences contain at least one head and the probability is 7/8. "1/2" comes from a solver who answers for a single flip and ignores that there are three. "3/4" comes from a solver who lists only HHH, HHT, HTT, and TTT as the possibilities and counts 3 of those 4. "2/3" comes from a solver who takes the probability of no heads to be 1/3 — one chance among the three flips — and subtracts that from 1.

distractor_solve.1/2: var heads=1, faces=2; return heads + "/" + faces;
distractor_solve.3/4: var fav=3, listed=4; return fav + "/" + listed;
distractor_solve.2/3: var num=3-1, den=3; return num + "/" + den;

subskill: interquartile range of an eight-value list
prompt: The eight values below are listed in increasing order: 3, 7, 8, 12, 14, 18, 21, 25. What is the interquartile range of these values?
explanation: The lower half is 3, 7, 8, 12, so Q1 = (7 + 8)/2 = 7.5; the upper half is 14, 18, 21, 25, so Q3 = (18 + 21)/2 = 19.5. The interquartile range is 19.5 - 7.5 = 12. "22" is 25 - 3, the full range rather than the interquartile range. "13" is (12 + 14)/2, the median of all eight values. "19.5" is Q3 by itself, reported before subtracting Q1.

subskill: scaling a sample rate to a population
prompt: A survey found that 3 out of every 8 students at a school ride the bus. At that rate, how many of the school's 1,240 students ride the bus?
explanation: Three eighths of the students ride the bus, and 1,240(3/8) = 465 students. "155" is 1,240/8, the size of one eighth, reported before multiplying by 3. "372" is 1,240(0.30), from a solver who reads "3 out of every 8" as 30 percent. "413" is 1,240/3 rounded, from a solver who divides by the 3 instead of by the 8.

"50%" is 15/30, from a solver who divides by the 30 books of January and February rather than by the five-month total.
